minors.title: live_sessions()/session_alive() add an undocumented ConnectTimeout option
minors.detail: The ticket pins the exact command `ssh -o BatchMode=yes <host> "tmux ls -F '#S' 2>/dev/null; true"`. jobs/registry.py's `_remote_shell` (line 446) builds `["ssh", "-o", "BatchMode=yes", "-o", "ConnectTimeout=5", host, script]`, adding a `ConnectTimeout=5` option not in the ticket's pinned invocation. This is extra functionality beyond the spec; it does not change fail-closed semantics (a stalled connect just fails faster, within the existing `timeout=20.0` bound) so the impact is low, but it is a deviation from the literal command the ticket specifies.

minors.title: _known_sessions() reads every historical run's meta.json on every ls() call
minors.detail: _known_sessions(all_entries) (added around line 795) calls _pieces_of(run_dir, start) - which opens and JSON-parses that run's meta.json - for every entry in the whole ledger, not just the rows this ls() call will display, and not gated by the workflow/debug filters. This adds an unbounded per-call disk-I/O cost (one meta.json read per run ever recorded) to every ls() invocation, growing without bound as the ledger accumulates runs, where previously ls() only read meta.json for the rows actually being folded and shown.

minors.title: Synthetic orphan row uses a verdict string outside the pinned six-verdict enum
minors.detail: _orphan_session_row (added around line 786) sets its piece's `verdict` to the literal string "orphan". Contracts 8.5 pins judge()/judge_service() to exactly six verdicts (done, dead, suspected stall, warming up, slowed, healthy); nothing in the ticket or contracts sanctions a seventh verdict value. A future caller that switches on the pinned verdict set (e.g. ticket 14's run.py ls renderer) will need an unplanned special case for this row. The implementer's own report already flags this as an open, unpinned design choice, but it is a new problem introduced by this diff and not yet resolved.
